raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Problem and change

The five randomized backward suites stop at 8192 tokens although their references already walk KV blocks. Raising the limits alone introduces 20 OOMs in the 512-case f16 dense suite on GH200: deterministic backward workspace and dBias still scale with `b*h_q*s_q*s_kv`.

Raise both sequence caps to 16384 in the f16 dense/THD, fp8 dense/THD and mxfp8 dense suites. Before drawing per-batch lengths, reduce the batch of an oversized draw to keep score cells within the previous suite maximum (`16*8*8192^2` for f16, `4*8*8192^2` for fp8/mxfp8). Sequence lengths, seeds and comparison tolerances remain unchanged; model-specific suite limits remain unchanged.

The wider sweep also exposed a backward-reference rounding problem that occurs under the old 8k limits. Combining a large row maximum with `log(normalizer)` in FP32 loses low bits; reconstructing `P=exp(S-LSE)` can then move dS across a half-precision rounding boundary and amplify the dK difference. Keep the row maximum and shifted normalizer separate, computing `P=exp(S-max)/normalizer`, including the sink probability. Twelve regression cases check equal logits beside half rounding boundaries and exact sink probabilities.

Related to #965. The Blackwell validation requested there remains outstanding; this contribution records Hopper coverage without treating architecture skips as passes.

## Validation

Base: `ddf1dd36007633710c468f7fef1acb3897d7f6f4`; one GH200, approximately 95 GiB visible HBM; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CuTeDSL 4.8.1. The seven changed files were matched by SHA256 against the remote test sources.

Full frozen sweep: **1277 passed / 1167 skipped / 0 failed**, in 2813.43 seconds (46:53). The longest call was 9.57 seconds, below the run's stricter 300-second watchdog and the repository's default 1500-second deadline.

| File group | Passed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| f16 backward | 1248 | 32 |
| fp8 backward | 17 | 751 |
| mxfp8 backward | 0 | 384 |
| new reference regressions | 12 | 0 |

From `test/python`:
```sh
CUDNN_FRONTEND_CUDART_LIB_NAME=libcudart.so.13 CUDNN_TEST_TIMEOUT=300 \
python -m pytest -n1 -rA --durations=20 \
  sdpa/graph/test_sdpa_backward_reference.py \
  sdpa/graph/suites/bprop/test_bprop_f16.py \
  sdpa/graph/suites/bprop/test_bprop_fp8.py \
  sdpa/graph/suites/bprop/test_bprop_mxfp8.py
```

Collected report archive SHA256: `3345ec089cb0f017db03f4cba813dea051671cc37d43cd76914210cedc96f9b9`; all 31 report/source files verified after collection. Captured large diagnostic arrays remain on the execution host and are not part of that small report archive.

Negative controls were retained:

- Raising caps without the joint bound: f16 1228 passed / 31 skipped / 21 failed (20 OOM, one numerical mismatch).
- Joint bound with the old reference: f16 1247 passed / 32 skipped / one numerical mismatch (`THD test492`).
- Original 8k baseline: f16 1247 passed / 32 skipped / one numerical mismatch (`THD test560`). These are different cases, not proof of equivalent failures.
- Captured inputs from those two numerical cases and the uncapped dense `test171` were checked with an independent FP64 calculation. All three pass with the stable normalization and the original comparison tolerances.

The fp8 suite has limited native Hopper support; mxfp8 requires SM100+ and is skipped. No B300 run is claimed. `pre-commit run --files` passed Black, Black-Jupyter and SPDX checks; there are no changed C++ files.

## Affected area and compatibility

CI/test infrastructure; no public API or supported-architecture changes.

## Before submitting

- [x] Contribution uses the repository's LICENSE.txt terms.
- [x] `pre-commit run --files` passed for the changed files.
- [x] Reviewed the applicable AGENTS.md rules.
- [ ] Requested labels: `cat-enhancements`, `area:global_attention`, `orig-external`. GitHub rejected label application for the author account; a maintainer needs to apply them.

+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sdpa.fp16_ref import compute_ref_backward
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L0
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("score", [-256.0, -128.0, 128.0, 256.0])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+def test_backward_reference_large_equal_scores(score, dtype):
+    """Equal logits have exact P=1/2, even beside a half rounding boundary."""
+    q = torch.tensor([[[[score]]]], device="cuda")
+    k = torch.ones((1, 1, 2, 1), device="cuda")
+    step = torch.finfo(dtype).eps
+    v = torch.tensor([[[[1.0 + step], [-1.0]]]], device="cuda")
+    o = torch.full_like(q, step / 2)
+    dq, dk, dv, _, _ = compute_ref_backward(q, k, v, o, torch.ones_like(o), torch_type=dtype)
+
+    # dS=(V-O)/2 lands exactly halfway between adjacent values. The reference
+    # deliberately rounds dS to the input type before its gradient GEMMs.
+    ds = ((v.double() - o.double()) / 2).to(dtype).double()
+    expected_dk = (ds * score).to(dtype).float()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(dq, torch.zeros_like(dq), rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(dk, expected_dk, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(dv, torch.full_like(dv, 0.5), rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L0
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("score", [-256.0, -128.0, 128.0, 256.0])
+def test_backward_reference_large_equal_scores_with_sink(score):
+    """The sink and two equal KV logits each have probability exactly 1/3."""
+    q = torch.tensor([[[[score]]]], device="cuda")
+    k = torch.ones((1, 1, 2, 1), device="cuda")
+    v = torch.ones_like(k)
+    o = torch.full_like(q, 2 / 3)
+    sink = torch.full_like(q, score)
+    _, _, _, _, dsink = compute_ref_backward(q, k, v, o, torch.ones_like(o), sink_token=sink)
+    expected = (-o.double() / 3).float()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(dsink, expected, rtol=1e-7, atol=0)

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `57c8424edeef` against base `03794f1af946`.

Thank you for your contribution! The joint score-size bound preserves long-sequence coverage while limiting the batches before per-sequence lengths and tensor geometry are derived. Keeping the row maximum and shifted normalizer separate also fixes a demonstrable FP32 reference-rounding problem without relaxing tolerances. No actionable regression found; the additional bounded SM100 validation below complements the existing Hopper results.

Validation: Reviewed all seven changed files and the reference/mask and random-configuration call paths. Validated an isolated integration of this head onto develop 03794f1af946b3ddd84dbd203801d6211aaf896a, with source and native-extension origins checked. Audited all 2,432 deterministic configurations across the five affected suites: every B*Hq*Sq*Skv fits its declared budget, all 279 batch reductions match the uncapped draw, and padded/ragged per-batch length arrays match the reduced batch count. 1,278 draws exceed the previous 8,192 sequence cap. On SM100, all 12 new analytic reference cases passed. Replacing only the reference with unchanged develop made all 12 fail, confirming the tests detect the intended defect. Ten selected native long-sequence forward/backward cases passed: five FP16/BF16 dense/THD, two FP8 dense/THD and three MXFP8 dense. These include 16K-scale geometry and three cases whose batch count is reduced by the new bound. The routing report confirms actual backend execution. One additional FP8 bottom-right case correctly skipped for the documented sequence-alignment restriction; a supported dense FP8 case passed separately. Retained the existing origin/category/attention labels and Frontend 1.32.0 milestone; added the PR to the Frontend project. Reused existing current-head CI instead of starting a duplicate pipeline.

Limitations: This is focused SM100 qualification, not a full 2,432-case Blackwell numerical sweep. The standard Python CI target excludes sdpa/graph/suites, so its results should not be described as covering that full sweep. No runtime kernel or API changes are introduced here; serving-performance benchmarking was not applicable.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
